hook_text: Give two people the same box of circuit parts and a written description, and you get two different circuits. Give them a diagram, and they build the same one.
clip_script: A box of circuit parts. Cells: the pushers, about one and a half volts each, big or small. Join two, plus to minus, and you get three volts; that is a battery. Copper wires: the roads, wrapped in plastic so the charges stay in and your fingers stay safe. A switch: the gate. Resistors: the speed bumps, which also turn energy into heat; your kettle element is one. Now the language. A cell: long thin line, short thick line, the long one positive. A bulb: circle with a cross. A resistor: a rectangle. Draw the wires straight, with a ruler, in a rectangle, and never leave a gap unless a switch is open. Current flows from positive, round the loop, back to negative. Learn these few symbols, and you can read any circuit in the world.
visual_style: A whiteboard spread of real-looking parts that morph one by one into their standard symbols, then snap together into a neat rectangular circuit diagram with a current arrow.
pacing: Quick part-by-part reveals, then a satisfying final diagram.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your first circuit diagram.
